claims.claim: the canal lifts ships about 26 meters above sea level to Gatun Lake
claims.definition: the lock staircase raises vessels roughly 26 m from ocean level to the level of Gatun Lake, the canal's summit water body
claims.measured_value: approximately 26 m (about 85 ft) above sea level
claims.authoritative_source: Panama Canal Authority (ACP) — how the canal works
claims.notes: narration and pop state twenty-six meters

claims.claim: terrain and tide made a sea-level canal impractical
claims.definition: the continental spine at the Culebra Cut is hard rock, the Chagres River had to be controlled, and the Pacific tide swings several meters; a sea-level channel was rejected after the French failure
claims.measured_value: Pacific tidal range on the order of meters; Culebra Cut through rock
claims.authoritative_source: David McCullough, The Path Between the Seas; Panama Canal Authority history
sources: McCullough, The Path Between the Seas
claims.notes: narration stays qualitative: hard rock, tide swings meters

claims.claim: the locks fill and empty by gravity from Lake Gatun, with no pumps
claims.definition: water flows through culverts and valves from the higher lake into the chambers; gravity alone moves every drop
claims.measured_value: no pumping in the fill/empty cycle
claims.authoritative_source: Panama Canal Authority — how the locks work

claims.claim: each ship transit discharges millions of liters of freshwater to the ocean
claims.definition: lockage water is freshwater from Gatun; each full transit releases on the order of 200 million liters (about 52 million US gallons) to the seas with the older locks
claims.measured_value: order of 200 million liters per transit (older locks); narration stays at 'millions of liters'
claims.authoritative_source: Panama Canal Authority water program; MIT Technology Review coverage of canal water use
claims.notes: freshwater, not seawater, is lost each transit; refill depends on rainfall in the watershed

claims.claim: drought lowers Gatun Lake and forces the canal to restrict drafts and daily transits
claims.definition: during the 2023-24 El Nino drought the canal imposed draft limits and cut daily booking slots as the lake fell
claims.measured_value: 2023-24: daily transits cut from ~36 toward the low 20s at the drought's worst; draft limits imposed
claims.authoritative_source: Panama Canal Authority advisories 2023-24; Reuters coverage
claims.notes: narration: cut drafts and daily transits; queue waits on rainfall

claims.claim: the post-2016 locks use water-saving basins that reuse about 60 percent of each lockage
claims.definition: the Neopanamax locks have paired basins that capture a majority of the chamber water and return it on the next cycle
claims.measured_value: approximately 60 percent of lockage water reused per transit
claims.authoritative_source: Panama Canal Authority — new locks water-saving basins
claims.notes: narration and pop state about sixty percent
